From 17b35355c2c6a761eaf571d63dab7f06b62249fb Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Arnd Bergmann <arnd@arndb.de>
Date: Wed, 3 Apr 2024 10:06:23 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] 3c515: remove unused 'mtu' variable

This has never been used since the start of the git history. When building
with W=1, the unused variable produces a gcc warning:

drivers/net/ethernet/3com/3c515.c:35:18: error: 'mtu' defined but not used [-Werror=unused-const-variable=]

Just remove it.

Fixes: 1da177e4c3f4 ("Linux-2.6.12-rc2")
Signed-off-by: Arnd Bergmann <arnd@arndb.de>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20240403080702.3509288-6-arnd@kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

diff --git a/drivers/net/ethernet/3com/3c515.c b/drivers/net/ethernet/3com/3c515.c
index ba3e7aa1a28f..4725a8cfd695 100644
--- a/drivers/net/ethernet/3com/3c515.c
+++ b/drivers/net/ethernet/3com/3c515.c
@@ -31,9 +31,6 @@
    Setting to > 1512 effectively disables this feature. */
 static int rx_copybreak = 200;
 
-/* Allow setting MTU to a larger size, bypassing the normal ethernet setup. */
-static const int mtu = 1500;
-
 /* Maximum events (Rx packets, etc.) to handle at each interrupt. */
 static int max_interrupt_work = 20;
 
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/net/ethernet/3com/3c515.c`**
- The unused variable `mtu`, which was defined as a constant integer with a value of 1500, has been removed from the code. This variable was never utilized in the codebase since its introduction.

### Relationships
- The removal of the `mtu` variable addresses a warning generated by the GCC compiler when building with the `W=1` option, which flags unused variables as errors. This change improves code cleanliness and eliminates unnecessary warnings during compilation. The patch is linked to a previous commit (1da177e4c3f4) that introduced the variable, indicating that the variable has been redundant since its inception.
